title: Let's shape your wedding
subtitle: Eight quick questions. You can change any of it later.

date.title: When's the big day?
date.help: Not sure yet? Pick a rough date and mark it flexible. We'll still build a usable timeline.
date.label: Wedding date

location.title: Where are you getting married?
location.help: Location matters more than you'd think. Marriage-license, waiting-period, and officiant rules depend on the ceremony jurisdiction and issuing office.

type.title: What kind of wedding?
type.help: This changes how much there is to plan. An elopement skips a lot.

option.traditionalHint: Ceremony plus reception, the full guest list
option.elopementHint: Just the two of you, maybe witnesses
option.courthouseHint: Civil ceremony, possibly a party later

guests.title: How many people?
guests.help: The US average is about 117 guests. A rough number is fine, it drives venue size and catering.

style.title: What should it feel like?
style.help: Pick as many as you like. This shapes vendor and decor suggestions, not your options.

venue.title: Any venue types in mind?
venue.help: All-inclusive venues bundle catering, rentals, and coordination, which removes a lot of separate tasks.

budget.title: What are you working with?
budget.help: The 2026 US average is about {average}, or roughly {perGuest} a guest. This is a starting point, not a ceiling.
budget.capacityLabel: How much planning time fits in a normal week?
budget.capacityHint: Count both of you together. Bliss uses this to avoid quietly overloading your evenings.
budget.plannerLabel: Are you working with a planner?
budget.plannerHint: A venue coordinator works for the venue, not for you. You still own most of the planning.

cultures.title: Any traditions you're bringing in?
cultures.help: About one in four US couples blends two traditions. Pick any that apply and we'll add the right events, vendors, and lead times.
cultures.none: None of these, or we'll decide later

conversation.title: Let's start where
conversation.intro: You do not have to answer like a planner. Start with what feels true; Bliss will turn it into a path only when it helps.
conversation.thinking: Thinking about what you just said…
conversation.skipped: We can leave that open. Nothing useful depends on forcing an answer today.
conversation.finishedPlaceholder: You have shared enough to begin
conversation.note: Nothing here is locked in. Bliss only records what you confirm.
conversation.finishedNote: You can keep talking in your workspace. Everything here remains editable.
conversation.error: Your starting point could not be saved. Check your connection and try again.

feeling.question: Before dates or lists: when you picture the day from the inside—not how it looks—what do you hope the two of you feel?
feeling.reply: I'm hearing “{answer}.” I'll use that as a compass when choices get noisy, not as a theme you have to defend.
feeling.claimNote: A compass for later choices, not a theme to lock in.

date.question: Looking ahead, is there already a date or season in view, or does the calendar still feel completely open?
date.reply: “{answer}” gives us enough of a horizon. I'll tell you when timing changes a choice; until then, nothing needs to feel urgent.
date.claimNote: Bliss schedules from this only after you confirm it.

place.question: Is there a place pulling you already—a city, a region, somewhere near family—or is that open too?
place.reply: I'll hold “{answer}” as a direction, not a commitment. Local rules and venue information can wait until the place is real enough to need them.
place.claimNote: Brings in local and legal information only when it becomes relevant.

people.question: When you imagine the room around you, does it feel small and close, lively and generous, or is guest count something you see differently?
people.reply: That gives the celebration a shape without turning anyone into a number. “{answer}” is enough for now.
people.claimNote: A planning range, not a final guest count.

support.question: One last thing: when planning gets complicated, what kind of help would feel most supportive from Bliss?
support.reply: I can do that: {answer}. I'll keep this as a preference you can change, and I won't confuse being helpful with taking over.
support.claimNote: Bliss uses this to pace questions and recommendations.

chips.next: Give us one clear next step
chips.options: Bring options, then let us talk

knows.title: What Bliss knows
knows.body: Every line came from something one of you said. Correct anything that is wrong—corrections stick.
knows.empty: Nothing yet. This fills in as you talk.

chapters.title: The fourteen chapters
chapters.body: Answering here quietly opens the chapters this affects. None become work until you decide something.

done.title: That is plenty to start
done.body: Bliss has enough to be useful. What you shared arrives as an editable starting point, not a locked decision.
done.action: See what carries into our workspace →

generating.title: Building your plan…
generating.body: Laying out your quests and working backward from {date}.
